cohort: The study reviewed 365,207 TREC-NBS from October 2011 to December 2014, identifying 467 newborns with abnormal screens (without PIDD) who were matched to controls.
finding: Infants with abnormal TREC-NBS, particularly unresolved or late abnormal TREC-NBS, had higher mortality even when primary immunodeficiency disorders (PIDD) were ruled out.
birth_weight: variable, used for matching controls and noted to be lower in infants with late abnormal TREC-NBS
gest_age: variable, used for matching controls and noted as severe prematurity in infants with late abnormal TREC-NBS
